1.word_for_word: daśame — in the tenth chapter; apātayat — He caused to fall; riṅgan — crawling; antarā yamala-arjunau — between the twin arjuna trees; tatratyābhyām devābhyām — by the two divine beings who were there; kṛṣṇaḥ stutaḥ — Kṛṣṇa was praised; iti īryate — this is narrated; yad vigarhitam karma — what reprehensible act; yena vā — or by what act; devarṣeḥ — of the divine sage; bhāgavata-uttamasya api — even of that foremost devotee; tamaḥ krodhaḥ — anger; tad etat kathyatām — let that matter be told.
1.translation: In the tenth chapter Kṛṣṇa, crawling between the twin arjuna trees, caused them to fall and was then praised by the two divine beings who had dwelt there. The king asks: what reprehensible act had they committed, or what was it that brought anger even to the divine sage Nārada, the foremost of devotees? Let that whole matter be told.

4.word_for_word: gaṅgāyām antar madhye — within the Gaṅgā, in its midst; kathaṃ-bhūte — of what kind?; ambhojānām vanāni — groves of lotuses; teṣām rājayaḥ — rows of those groves; tāḥ vidyante yasmin — in which such rows existed.
4.translation: 'Within the Gaṅgā' means in its midst. The river is described as one in which there were rows upon rows of lotus groves.

5.word_for_word: apaśyat — he saw them; dṛṣṭvā ca — and having seen them; kṣībāṇau — intoxicated; mattau — drunk; samabudhyata — he understood them to be so.
5.translation: Nārada saw the two and, on seeing them, understood that they were intoxicated and drunk.

6.word_for_word: kutaḥ — why was this so?; iti ataḥ āha — to explain, the verse says; tam dṛṣṭvā — 'seeing him.'
6.translation: To explain why the women covered themselves while the two men did not, the verse says, 'seeing him.'

7.word_for_word: anugraha-arthāya — for the purpose of showing favor; anugrahaḥ ca — the favor consisted in; mada-nāśaḥ — the destruction of their pride/intoxication; arthaḥ ca — and its further purpose was; śrī-kṛṣṇa-darśanam — the sight of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; tad-artham — for that purpose; idam vakṣyamāṇam — he spoke what follows; na hi anya iti-ādi — beginning with 'there is indeed no other.'
7.translation: Nārada intended the curse as an act of favor. That favor consisted first in destroying their pride and intoxication, and further in bringing them to the vision of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. For this purpose he spoke the words that follow, beginning, 'There is indeed no other...'

8.word_for_word: joṣyān — pleasurable objects; priyān viṣayān — beloved sense objects; juṣataḥ — of a person enjoying them; sevamānasya puṃsaḥ — of one who serves or indulges them; śrī-madāt anya ābhijātya-ādiḥ madaḥ — apart from pride born of wealth, other prides arise from noble birth, learning and the like; anyaḥ vā rajo-guṇaḥ — nor is some other rājasic condition; rajaḥ-kārya-hāsya-harṣa-ādi-rūpaḥ — such as laughter, excitement and the other effects of rajas; na hi — not the true cause; buddhi-bhraṃśaḥ — the collapse of discernment; buddhiṃ bhraṃśayati — that which makes intelligence fall; kintu śrī-madaḥ eva — rather, pride of wealth itself is the cause; yatra — in which, namely in the pride of wealth.
8.translation: For a person absorbed in pleasurable sense objects, the decisive cause of the collapse of discernment is pride born of wealth. Other forms of pride, such as those produced by high birth or learning, and other manifestations of rajas such as laughter and excitement, are not being singled out here as the principal cause. Rather, the verse points specifically to the intoxication of wealth; the following verses explain what occurs within that condition.

9.word_for_word: imam naśvaram deham — this perishable body; ajarā-mṛtyu — as though free from old age and death; ajaraḥ ca amṛtyuḥ ca yathā — regarding it as if it neither aged nor died; tathā manyamānaiḥ — by those who think in that way.
9.translation: Although this body is perishable, such people regard it as though it were free from old age and death—as though it neither aged nor died.

10.word_for_word: nara-deva-bhūdeva-saṃjñitam api — although it may be designated 'king,' 'god among men,' or 'brāhmaṇa'; śvā-ādibhiḥ bhakṣitam — when eaten by dogs and other animals; viṭ-saṃjñitam — it is called excrement; dagdham — when burned; bhasma-saṃjñitam — it is called ashes; anyadā kṛmi-saṃjñitam — otherwise it becomes worms; tat-kṛte tad-artham — for the sake of that body; yaḥ bhūta-dhruk — one who harms living beings; bhūta-droghdā — an injurer of creatures; yataḥ bhūta-drohāt nirayaḥ bhavati — because harming living beings leads to hell; sa kim svārtham veda — does he understand his own true welfare?; na eva veda — he certainly does not.
10.translation: A body may now be designated a king, a 'god among men,' or a brāhmaṇa; yet when eaten by dogs and other creatures it becomes excrement, when burned it becomes ashes, and otherwise it becomes worms. A person who harms living beings for the sake of such a body does not understand his own welfare at all, for hostility toward living beings leads to hell.

11.word_for_word: idānīm — now; dehe aham-bhāvaḥ api — even the notion 'I am this body'; na ghaṭate — cannot be made coherent; iti āha — he says; dehaḥ iti — with the verse beginning 'the body'; niṣektuḥ — of the one who deposits the seed; pituḥ — the father; mātuḥ pituḥ vā — or of the mother's father; mātāmahasya — the maternal grandfather; putrikā-karaṇe — in the arrangement by which a daughter is appointed to produce an heir.
11.translation: Nārada now shows that even the notion 'I am this body' cannot be coherently maintained. 'The one who deposits the seed' is the father. 'Or of the mother's father' refers to the maternal grandfather in the arrangement in which a daughter is appointed to produce an heir for her father's line.

12.word_for_word: avyakta-prabhava-apyayam — arising from the unmanifest and dissolving back into that very unmanifest; avyaktāt prabhavaḥ — whose origin is from the unmanifest; tasmin eva apyayaḥ — whose dissolution is into that same source; ātmāsāt-kṛtvā — appropriating as oneself; ātmā iti matvā — thinking 'this is myself'; asataḥ mūḍhāt ṛte — except for an unrealized fool.
12.translation: The body arises from the unmanifest and dissolves back into that same unmanifest source. Who, other than a deluded person, would appropriate such a body as the self—thinking 'this is I'—and then kill other creatures for its sake?

13.word_for_word: evam śrī-mada-viceṣṭitam uktvā — having described the conduct produced by intoxication with wealth; tat-pratīkāram niścinoti — he determines its remedy; asataḥ iti — beginning with 'of the unwise'; param — supreme, best; dāridryam eva kevalam — or, poverty alone; kutaḥ — why?; ātma-aupamyena — by comparison with oneself; tataḥ na druhyati — therefore the poor person does not harm others.
13.translation: Having described the behavior produced by intoxication with wealth, Nārada determines its remedy. 'Param' means the best remedy—or it may mean that poverty alone is that remedy. Why? Because through comparison with oneself the poor person understands the suffering of others and therefore does not injure them.

14.word_for_word: sa-dṛṣṭāntam āha — he gives an illustration; yathā iti — with the verse beginning 'just as'; mukha-amlānya-ādi-liṅgaiḥ — from signs such as a dejected face; sarveṣām jīvānām sukha-duḥkhe same — happiness and suffering are alike for all living beings; iti jñātavān — he comes to know this.
14.translation: He illustrates the point. From signs such as another person's dejected face, one who has suffered himself recognizes that happiness and pain are alike for all living beings.

15.word_for_word: kiṃ ca — moreover; dāridryam mokṣam api sādhayati — poverty can also become a means to liberation; iti āha — he says this; daridra iti śloka-catuṣṭayena — in the four verses beginning 'the poor man'; nirahaṃ-stambhaḥ — free from the rigidity of ego; nirgataḥ ahaṅkāra-rūpaḥ stambhaḥ yasmāt — one from whom the stiffness called egoism has departed.
15.translation: Moreover, poverty can also become a means to liberation; Nārada explains this in the four verses beginning 'the poor man.' 'Nirahaṃ-stambha' means one from whom the rigidity or stiff pride that is egoism has departed.

17.word_for_word: yujyante — they become connected; svataḥ eva saṅgacchante — saintly persons naturally associate with him; tarṣam — thirst; tṛṣṇām — craving.
17.translation: Saintly persons naturally come into association with the poor man. 'Tarṣa' means thirst or craving. Through the company of the saints that craving is diminished.

18.word_for_word: nanu — objection; sādhūnām api dhanikaḥ priyaḥ syāt na daridraḥ — perhaps even saints prefer a wealthy person rather than a poor one; tatra āha — to this he says; sādhūnām iti — with the verse beginning 'of the saints'; dhanena stambhaḥ garvaḥ yeṣām — those whose stiffness or pride is produced by wealth.
18.translation: One might object that even saintly people would prefer the wealthy rather than the poor. Nārada answers with the verse beginning 'of the saints.' The expression refers to people whose pride and rigid arrogance are produced by wealth; such people are precisely those whom equal-minded saints have no reason to court.

19.word_for_word: tamo-madam — the intoxication arising from darkness/ignorance; ajñāna-kṛtam madam — pride produced by ignorance.
19.translation: 'Tamo-mada' means intoxicated pride produced by ignorance.

20.word_for_word: tamaḥ-plutau — submerged in darkness; tamo-vyāptau — covered by ignorance.
20.translation: 'Tamaḥ-plutau' means that the two were submerged in darkness, covered by ignorance.

21.word_for_word: śapati — he curses them; ataḥ arhataḥ iti — with the words 'therefore you deserve'; anugṛhṇāti — yet he also favors them; syātām na evam iti-ādinā — beginning with 'let it not be so again'; mat-prasādena smṛtiḥ syāt — by my grace, let remembrance remain.
21.translation: Nārada curses them with the words 'therefore you deserve [immobility],' yet in the very curse he also favors them, beginning with 'let it not be so again.' By his grace, their remembrance and awareness would remain even in that condition.

22.word_for_word: svar-lokatām — the state of dwelling in heaven; devatvam — divine status; punaḥ labdhvā — having obtained it again; mad-anugrahāt — by my grace; labdha-bhaktī bhaviṣyataḥ — the two will possess devotion.
22.translation: After again obtaining divine status and residence in heaven, the two would, by Nārada's grace, possess devotion.

24.word_for_word: prastutam āha — he returns to the matter at hand; ṛṣeḥ iti — with the verse beginning 'of the sage.'
24.translation: Śuka now returns to the matter at hand with the verse beginning 'of the sage.'

25.word_for_word: kim iti satyam kartavyam — why must the sage's words be made true?; tatra āha — to this He says; devarṣiḥ iti — 'the divine sage'; yad — because, since; yataḥ — because; tat — therefore; tataḥ — for that reason.
25.translation: Why did Kṛṣṇa regard it as necessary to make the sage's words true? He answers, 'the divine sage is most dear to Me.' Here 'yad' has the force 'because,' and 'tat' therefore means 'for that reason.'

26.word_for_word: yamayoḥ — of the pair; yamalayoḥ — of the twins; sahaja-tayoḥ — born together; ātmanaḥ kṛṣṇasya — of Kṛṣṇa Himself; tan-madhya-praveśa-mātreṇa — merely by His entering between them.
26.translation: 'Yamayoḥ' means the pair, the twin trees born together. The mortar turned crosswise merely because Kṛṣṇa Himself entered between them.

27.word_for_word: anu añcati iti anvak — 'anvak' means following after; tatra hetuḥ — the reason is given; dāmodareṇa — by Dāmodara; utkalitaḥ — uprooted; utpāṭitaḥ — torn up; aṅghri-bandhaḥ — the bond of the feet, the root-fastening; mūla-bandhaḥ — the root base; yayoḥ tau — of the two trees; paramasya śrī-kṛṣṇasya vikramitam — the exertion/power of the Supreme Śrī Kṛṣṇa; tena ati-vepaḥ kampaḥ — by that, excessive trembling; yeṣu te skandha-pravāla-viṭapāḥ — whose trunks, shoots and branches shook violently.
27.translation: 'Anvak' means following behind. The cause of the trees' fall is Dāmodara: their foot-bonds, that is, their roots, were uprooted. Through the exertion of the Supreme Śrī Kṛṣṇa, their trunks, shoots and branches trembled violently before they crashed down.

28.word_for_word: kakubhaḥ prati — toward the directions; sarvataḥ sphurantau — shining on every side; yad vā — alternatively; diśaḥ prakāśayantau — illuminating the directions; kujayoḥ vṛkṣayoḥ sthitaḥ agniḥ yathā mūrtim anupaiti tathā upetya — as fire dwelling in two pieces of wood assumes visible form, so they emerged from the trees; virajasau — free from rajas; nirmadau — free from intoxication/pride; nirahaṅkāriṇau — without egoism; naṣṭa-garvau — their arrogance destroyed.
28.translation: The two shone in every direction—or, alternatively, illuminated the directions. Just as fire hidden within two pieces of wood comes forth in visible form, the two divine beings emerged from the trees. 'Virajasau' means that they were free of passion and intoxicated pride, without egoism, their arrogance destroyed.

29.word_for_word: gopālam mām yuvām devau kim iti praṇatau — objection: why do you two gods bow to Me, a cowherd?; tatra āhatuḥ — to this they reply; he kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-yogin — O Kṛṣṇa, O great master of yoga; acintya-prabhāvaḥ tvam — Your power is inconceivable; na gopālaḥ — You are not merely a cowherd; kintu paraḥ puruṣaḥ — but the Supreme Person; yataḥ ādyaḥ — because You are primordial; kāraṇa-bhūtaḥ — the causal source; na nimitta-mātram — not merely the efficient cause; kintu upādānam api tvam eva — You are also the material cause; vyakta-avyaktam — the manifest and unmanifest; sthūla-sūkṣmam idam — this gross and subtle universe; te rūpam viduḥ — the brāhmaṇas know as Your form.
29.translation: One might ask why two gods would bow to Kṛṣṇa if He were merely a cowherd. They answer: 'O Kṛṣṇa, great master of yoga, Your power is inconceivable. You are not merely a cowherd but the Supreme Person, the primordial causal source.' He is not only the efficient cause; He is also the material cause. Thus the brāhmaṇas know this whole manifest and unmanifest, gross and subtle universe to be His form.

30.word_for_word: niyantā api tvam eva — You alone are also the controller; tvam ekaḥ iti — therefore they say 'You alone'; dehaḥ — the body; asavaḥ — the vital airs; prāṇāḥ — life-breaths; ātmā ahaṅkāraḥ — 'self' here means ego; indriyāṇi ca — and the senses; teṣām īśvaraḥ — You are the ruler of all these; nanu — objection; asya kālaḥ nimittam — time may be the efficient cause of this universe; prakṛtiḥ upādānam — prakṛti may be its material cause; prakṛteḥ jātaḥ mahān — mahat arises from prakṛti; viśva-ātmatayā pariṇamate — it transforms into the cosmic totality; puruṣaḥ kartā niyantā ca — and puruṣa may be the agent and controller; kim atra aham — why then identify all this with You?; tvam eva kālaḥ — You Yourself are Time; yataḥ bhagavān īśvaraḥ viṣṇuḥ tvam — because You are Bhagavān, Lord Viṣṇu, the sovereign; ataḥ kālaḥ nāma tava līlā — therefore what is called Time is Your own līlā.
30.translation: They further say that He alone is the controller. He is the Lord of the body, the vital airs, ego and the senses. One might object that Time is the efficient cause, prakṛti the material cause, mahat arises from prakṛti and develops into the cosmic totality, while puruṣa is the agent and controller—so why identify all these with Kṛṣṇa? Their answer is: You Yourself are Time. Because You are Bhagavān, the sovereign Viṣṇu, what is called Time is itself Your līlā.

31.word_for_word: prakṛtiḥ śaktiḥ — prakṛti is Your power; puruṣaḥ aṃśaḥ — puruṣa is Your portion; mahān kāryam — mahat is Your effect; ataḥ tvam eva sarvam — therefore You alone are everything.
31.translation: Prakṛti is His power, puruṣa is His portion, and mahat is His effect. Therefore He alone is all of these.

32.word_for_word: nanu aham eva cet sarvam — objection: if I alone am everything; tarhi ghaṭa-ādi-jñāne mat-jñānam kim na bhavati — why does knowledge of a pot and other objects not amount to knowledge of Me?; bhavati iti cet — if it does; sarvaḥ api brahma-vit syāt — then everyone would be a knower of Brahman; ataḥ āhatuḥ — therefore they say; gṛhyamāṇaiḥ iti — with 'by things that are grasped'; dṛśyatvena vartamānaiḥ — existing as objects of perception; buddhi-ahaṅkāra-indriya-ādibhiḥ — by intellect, ego, senses and the rest; draṣṭā tvam na gṛhyase — You, the seer, are not grasped; jīvaḥ jānātu — objection: then perhaps the jīva can know You; na eva — no; ko nu iha — 'who indeed here?'; jīva-ādi-utpatteḥ prāk eva — even before the arising of the jīva and the rest; sva-prakāśatayā siddham tvām — You are established as self-luminous; guṇa-saṃvṛtaḥ — one covered by the guṇas; deha-ādi-āvṛtaḥ — veiled by body and the rest; kaḥ vā jānāti — who can know You?
32.translation: One might object: if He is everything, why does knowledge of a pot or any other object not itself constitute knowledge of Him? If it did, everyone would automatically be a knower of Brahman. The answer is that intellect, ego, senses and other natural modifications are themselves objects of perception, whereas He is the seer and cannot be grasped by those objects. Nor can the conditioned jīva simply know Him, for He is self-luminous and established prior even to the arising of the jīva's empirical apparatus; one covered by the guṇas and veiled by body and the rest cannot comprehend Him.

33.word_for_word: ataḥ durjñeyatvāt — because He is so difficult to know; kevalam praṇamataḥ — they simply bow; tasmai tubhyam iti — with the words 'unto that You'; ātmanaḥ svasmāt — from Himself; dyotaḥ prakāśaḥ yeṣām — the guṇas whose illumination comes from Him; taiḥ guṇaiḥ channaḥ mahimā yasya — whose greatness is concealed by those guṇas; abhrair iva raveḥ — like the sun concealed by clouds.
33.translation: Because He is so difficult to know, they can only bow to Him. The guṇas themselves receive their illumination from Him, yet His greatness is concealed by those very guṇas, just as the sun is concealed by clouds.

34.word_for_word: aho aham īśvaraḥ iti kutaḥ jñānam — how, then, can there be knowledge that 'this indeed is the Lord'?; tatra āhatuḥ — to this they say; yasya iti — with the verse beginning 'whose descents are known.'
34.translation: How, then, is one to know that He is the Lord? They answer with the verse beginning, 'whose descents are known...' His extraordinary deeds reveal the otherwise bodiless Lord through His incarnate forms.

35.word_for_word: bhavāya — for arising, existence; udbhavāya — for bringing forth; vibhavāya — for that in which bhava is gone; vigataḥ bhavaḥ yasmin tasmai — for the state from which worldly becoming has departed; kaivalyāya — for liberation.
35.translation: 'Bhavāya' means for the arising and flourishing of the worlds. 'Vibhavāya' is interpreted as that in which worldly becoming has disappeared—that is, for liberation or kaivalya.

37.word_for_word: nau — us two; āvām — the two of us; anucaraḥ — follower; kuberaḥ nāradaḥ vā — either Kubera or Nārada is the 'follower' intended; tasya kiṅkarau — we are servants connected with him; bhagavataḥ tava darśanam — the sight of You, Bhagavān.
37.translation: 'Nau' means 'the two of us.' In calling themselves servants of Your follower, 'the follower' may refer to Kubera or to Nārada. Through the sage's favor the two of us obtained the vision of You, Bhagavān.

38.word_for_word: tatra gatayoḥ āvayoḥ — when the two of us go from here; pūrva-svabhāvaḥ viṣaya-pravaṇatā — let not our former nature, inclination toward sense objects, return; na it bahu-vacanam — the plural form is not literal for only two; asmad-o dvayoḥ ca iti dvi-vacana-sthāne bahu-vacanam — a plural can stand in place of the dual for 'us two'; asmat-saṅginām sarveṣām api — or the plural may include all our associates; tava nivāsa-bhūtam yat jagat — the world which is Your dwelling; tasya praṇāme — in bowing to it; tvat-nivāsa-bhūtam iti bahu-mānena — out of reverence because it is Your abode; jagataḥ praṇāme śiraḥ astu — let our heads bow to the world; bhavat-tanūnām — of Your bodies/forms; bhavataḥ mūrtīnām — of Your manifestations.
38.translation: Their prayer is that when they depart, their former nature—the inclination toward sense objects—will not return. The plural forms may stand for the dual 'we two,' or may intentionally include all of their associates. They pray that their heads bow to the whole world out of reverence because the world is His dwelling, and that their sight be fixed upon the saints as manifestations of His forms.

39.translation: 'Saṅkīrtitaḥ' here means thoroughly praised or extolled.

40.word_for_word: vāgbhiḥ — by the words; na hi anyaḥ juṣataḥ joṣyān iti-ādibhiḥ — beginning with 'there is indeed no other [cause of downfall] for one enjoying pleasurable objects'; śrī-vibhraṃśa-rūpaḥ anugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ — favor was bestowed in the form of the loss of their wealth.
40.translation: The Lord refers to Nārada's words beginning, 'There is indeed no other...' By those words the sage bestowed grace upon them in the form of their fall from wealth and the destruction of the pride that wealth had produced.

41.word_for_word: yuktam eva etat — this is entirely fitting; sādhūnām — of those who live according to true dharma; sva-dharma-vartinām — those established in their proper dharma; sama-cittānām — of the equal-minded; ātma-vidām — knowers of the Self; sutarām mat-kṛta-ātmanām — especially of those whose minds have been placed in Me; mayi arpita-cittānām — whose consciousness is offered to Me; teṣām kṛpā-atirekāt — because their compassion is especially great; sutarām iti uktam — therefore 'especially' is stated; savituḥ darśanāt akṣṇoḥ yathā bandhaḥ na bhavet — just as the sight of the sun does not bind the eyes; tadvat — so too the sight of the saints does not bind a person.
41.translation: This is entirely fitting. Saints are those established in true dharma, equal-minded knowers of the Self; and especially those whose minds are wholly offered to the Lord. Because the compassion of such devotees is extraordinarily great, the verse says 'especially.' Just as seeing the sun does not bind the eyes, seeing such saints does not create bondage in a person.

42.word_for_word: prādhānyāt ekasya sambodhanam — only one is addressed because one name is taken as representative; he nalakūvara — O Nalakūvara; yuvām — you two; tat tasmāt — therefore; sādanam sva-niketam — your own dwelling; mat-paramau santau — remaining devoted to Me as supreme; gacchatam — go; vām yuvayoḥ — for you two; apekṣitaḥ — the desired thing; mayi prema — love for Me; jātaḥ eva — has already arisen; abhavaḥ — that in which there is no bhava; na bhavaḥ yasmin saḥ — the supreme state in which worldly becoming does not recur.
42.translation: Only Nalakūvara is directly addressed, one name standing for the pair: 'O Nalakūvara, you two should therefore return to your own abode while remaining devoted to Me as supreme.' The thing you desired—love for Me—has already arisen in both of you. 'Abhava' denotes the supreme state in which worldly becoming no longer recurs.

43.word_for_word: baddha-ulūkhalam — He in whom the mortar was bound; baddham ulūkhalam yasmin tam — the One to whom the mortar remained tied.
43.translation: 'Baddholūkhalam' means Kṛṣṇa with the mortar still bound to Him.
